Varn Glacier

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Varn Glacier
LocationTarn Range, Norland
Area41.2 km²
Length14 km
TerminusVarn Lake
StatusRetreating

Varn Glacier is a valley glacier in the Tarn Range of Norland, flowing north from the Varn icefield into Varn Lake. It is about 14 kilometres long, and it is one of the most studied glaciers in the region, because a road reaches within two kilometres of its snout.[1]

The glacier has retreated by roughly 1.8 kilometres since systematic measurements began in 1931. Since 2024, it has been monitored by a network of forty seismic sensors, which record the cracking caused by meltwater under the ice.[2]

Geography

The glacier is fed by the Varn icefield, which lies at an elevation of between 1,600 and 2,100 metres. Two smaller tributary glaciers joined it from the east until the 1970s, when they separated, and they now end in steep icefalls above the main valley.

Research

The University of Tarn has run a field station near the glacier since 1962. Its long record of summer mass balance, taken with stakes drilled into the ice, is often used to check satellite estimates for the wider range.
